evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the Buzz Tone & Volume Expander as a UMI product made in the United States, while Gearphoria describes Richard Soloway founding UMI in 1967 and making pedals after first making amplifiers. A surviving 1968 example independently supports period manufacture.
Effects Database groups Apollo No. 843 with the UMI Buzz Tone & Volume Expander and identifies the Apollo state as UMI-built.
Effects Database identifies Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander as UMI-made and places it in the same related chain as Apollo, Kimberly, and UMI.

Effects Database explicitly separates Kimberly production into v1 by LIMMCO and v2 by Applied. Later related states include Apollo, Conrad, and UMI, so Kimberly must not be represented as a single-factory product.

Effects Database groups Audio Designs Fuzzound with Kimberly and the later UMI/Apollo/Conrad states as part of the same related design family, while maintaining Applied as the builder for the Audio Designs state.

Gearphoria states that UMI made a Tone Booster and that it also exists under different brand names, but the author did not identify who manufactured those alternate branded examples. Alternate labels therefore remain separate unresolved records rather than automatic UMI assignments.

Gearphoria documents the UMI Treble-Bass Booster & Mute as one of the company's pedal products, but provides less production dating and no independent factory documentation beyond the UMI product attribution.
Gearphoria documents the UMI Wa Pedal as an original UMI product and says Soloway began UMI with fuzz and wah products. Exact model dating remains less certain.
